newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia govt, Democrats reach labour agreement.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia govt, Democrats reach labour agreement.

text.p: The Australian government has reached agreement with the Australian Democrats on its plans to deregulate the labour market, ensuring passage of the laws through the upper house of parliament, the Senate.

Industrial Relations Minister Peter Reith said in a television interview on Sunday that some changes had been made to the government's Workplace Relations Bill but that it retained the integrity of the original bill.

"There are something like 181 amendments, some of them are very technical, that's true, but there are a lot of changes," Reith told the Nine Network's Sunday programme. The agreement, signed on Friday, between Reith and Democrats leader Cheryl Kernot followed more than 50 hours of negotiations over more than a month.
The legislation, a centrepiece of the coalition government's legislative programme, is aimed at reducing the influence of the union movement in the wage negotiating process.
The government has said it is crucial to reducing unemployment levels.

The government needs two non-government votes to pass its legislation in the Senate. The Democrats' support was vital as Labor, the Greens and independent senator Mal Colston oppose the Workplace Relations Bill.

Reith said the bill would meet the coalition's election pledge that no worker would be worse off and at the same time remove impediments to hiring workers, increase flexibility and promote economic growth.
He said the changes the bill implemented over time would encourage economic growth and that would increase employment.

Kernot said the bill met the government's policy goal of increasing flexibility but,with the changes secured during negotiations, also provided safeguards for vulnerable workers. "The government doesn't have everything it wants, we don't have everything we want, but it's supportable," Kernot told the Sunday programme.
